title: Multi-round Even--Mansour security with one identical key
summary: Determine the optimal query-security frontier for multi-round Even--Mansour with independent round permutations and the same key at every addition.

formal_statement.body: For every fixed integer $r>2$, consider the $r$-round Even--Mansour cipher with $r$ independent public random $n$-bit permutations and one uniformly random $n$-bit key reused in all $r+1$ key additions. Does the construction attain strong-PRP security up to $\widetilde O(2^{rn/(r+1)})$ adaptive two-sided queries? Prove the bound for every $r>2$, or give a compatible distinguishing attack that establishes a lower frontier. In particular, settle the source-emphasized $r=3$ threshold $2^{3n/4}$.

scope.domain: Information-theoretic strong-PRP security of multi-round Even--Mansour with correlated subkeys
assumptions: The r public random n-bit permutations are independent
The same uniformly random n-bit key is reused in all r+1 key additions
The adversary may query the cipher and public permutations adaptively in both directions
scope.unresolved_remainder: A later result proves that the natural two-constraint sum-capture proof route overcounts by $\Omega(q^3/N)$ for $r=3$, but explicitly does not provide a distinguisher. The $2^{3n/4}$ threshold and the full family for every $r>2$ remain unsettled.

progress.summary: The source asks for the optimal exponent with independent round permutations and one identical round key, highlighting three rounds as the first unresolved case.
A lower-bound construction shows that the anticipated two-constraint sum-capture proof route overcounts for three rounds, while explicitly leaving the cipher's security unresolved.
